description: prop:q-hecke-seminormal-character-closure publishes a five-nucleon trace table in the EXCISED convention C. The canonical Hoefsmit+Wenzl bridge witness computes those same five atoms by the block's own stated method (sum_lambda y_lambda chi_lambda) and agrees with none of them: proton 1.0755x, neutron 1.0699x, deuteron 1.4813x, tritium 2.2038x, 3He 1.9549x. The proton ratio is the signature qou-46ab proved to 50 digits (C-frame 1.0653062286131670594, D-frame 1.1457597822878355047, |D-C|/C = 0.0755215). The block's own 'relative error ~1e-15' column is agreement between two C-frame paths, which says nothing about which convention both are in. The same C value is live in QOU/Interactions/MarkovPeelH3.lean, claiming it 'matches Hoefsmit + Wenzl bridge witness atomic-tr-m-mpfr-50dps.witness.json to ~4e-16' when that witness gives 1.1457597823152389404 -- a 7.02e-2 gap, wrong by 14 orders of magnitude, and word-for-word the class qou-46ab fixed at canonical_tr_m_three_path_comparison.py:104. qou-46ab's sweep could not see either site: three renderings of one C-frame quantity share the prefix 1.0653062286 and diverge after it (scanned ...61316, block ...59, Lean ...592389333), and a literal scan matches none of the others -- so a sweep whose purpose was to find these returned zero for content and Lean. The block's declaring witness is a structural verifier over five ABSTRACT B_3 braids and cannot carry a nucleon table. NOTHING IS RECOMPUTED: the migration belongs to qou-46ab and moves five published figures by 7-120 %. qou-i229.

why_the_literal_scan_missed_it.note: same C-frame quantity, three renderings; a literal scan matches none of the others

caveats: NOTHING IS RECOMPUTED. Migrating this table to convention D is qou-46ab's scoped job; it moves five published figures by 7-120 % and needs the Lean declaration moved in the same pass or the two diverge further. Both sites are LABELLED, the precedent df13e845cee set.

No claim about the 11th-digit residual between the block's rendering (...59) and qou-46ab's C-frame (...61) -- that is 2e-11, a separate and much smaller question than the 7.55 % convention gap, and it is not diagnosed here.
No claim that the character-closure identity is wrong. It is not; the declaring probe verifies it correctly on abstract braids and it holds in either convention.
